record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Topology of Manifolds
record.original_question: For compact aspherical 4-manifolds with boundary, in the same setting where topological surgery applies to good fundamental groups, what groups can occur as the fundamental groups of the boundary components?

evidence.quote: One now proceeds to the following three problems: 1. Decide which good pi are the fundamental groups of compact aspherical 4-manifolds. 2. Determine the possible fundamental groups of the boundary components.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A topological 4-manifold M is called aspherical if its universal cover is contractible, equivalently if all its higher homotopy groups vanish. A discrete group π is called "good" (in the sense of topological surgery theory in dimension 4) if π satisfies the conditions under which the disk embedding theorem and topological surgery exact sequence hold; in particular, every group of subexponential growth, and more generally every elementary amenable group, is good.

Consider compact, connected, aspherical topological 4-manifolds M with nonempty boundary ∂M, whose fundamental group π₁(M) is a good group. Each component of ∂M is a closed 3-manifold whose fundamental group injects into π₁(M) (up to conjugacy, choosing basepoints).

Problem: Characterize precisely which groups arise as the fundamental group of a boundary component of such a manifold. That is, give a complete description of the class

G = { π₁(C) : C is a connected component of ∂M for some compact aspherical 4-manifold M with π₁(M) a good group }.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of determining which groups occur as fundamental groups of compact aspherical 4-manifolds, and which can appear as boundary fundamental groups, is generally listed as an open problem in the topology of 4-manifolds. Partial classification results exist for the case of elementary amenable fundamental groups (e.g., compact aspherical 4-manifolds with elementary amenable π₁ and connected boundary have been classified up to homeomorphism by the boundary data and inclusion-induced map), but a full characterization in the "good group" setting remains open.

status_evidence.title: Borel Conjecture for compact aspherical 4-manifolds - Manifold Atlas
status_evidence.snippet: Problems include deciding which good groups are fundamental groups of compact 4-manifolds and determining the possible boundary components.
status_evidence.claim: The classification of boundary fundamental groups for compact aspherical 4-manifolds with good fundamental groups is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: arXiv:2501.12512 — Aspherical 4-manifolds with elementary amenable fundamental group
status_evidence.snippet: Compact aspherical 4-manifolds with elementary amenable fundamental group π and connected nonempty boundary N are classified up to homeomorphism by π, N, and the inclusion-induced homomorphism.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist in the elementary amenable case, but a general classification of boundary groups is not provided.
